advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the 'Logging decision' section of infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md to reflect that the host docker.service journald stream (including review-bot) now ships off-box to /rebar/gerrit-host via infra/terraform/host_logs.tf.
evidence: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:141-142 review-bot service uses `logging: driver: journald`, so its output lands under docker.service and is now shipped off-box

infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:628-634 records 'DECISION: do not ship review-bot logs to a CloudWatch Logs group at this time' with the rationale that journald is reachable on demand and that off-box shipping is a future 'follow-up'
ticket rebar:9018-3385-ccfa-4568 description: 'docker.service (all 4 containers log there; confirmed ... for gerrit, review-bot, opcert and rebar-mcp)'
advisory.finding: The 'Logging decision' in infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md states review-bot logs are NOT shipped to CloudWatch (premise: on-demand journald access suffices), but this change ships the host's docker.service journald stream, which carries the review-bot container's logs, off-box to the /rebar/gerrit-host log group, making that recorded current-state statement inaccurate.
scenarios: An operator reading review-bot-ops.md after this change concludes review-bot logs are only in on-box journald and does not check /rebar/gerrit-host, missing the off-box copy now available.
advisory.suggested_fix: In infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:628-634, correct the current-state claim to note that since bug fab-dismal-haddock (9018-3385-ccfa-4568) the host's docker.service journald output, which includes the review-bot container, is shipped off-box to the /rebar/gerrit-host log group, so review-bot logs are now available in CloudWatch via the shared host group.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten or remove the wildcard logs:* grant in iam.tf cloudwatch_basic so the new host_logs_ship scoping to /rebar/gerrit-host is effective.
evidence: host_logs.tf:98-112 comment: 'The agent's log and config reads, scoped to this one group...' with resources = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group.gerrit_host.arn, "${...}:*"]
iam.tf:74-85: data "aws_iam_policy_document" "cloudwatch_basic" grants actions logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, logs:PutLogEvents with resources = ["*"]
iam.tf:87-91: aws_iam_role_policy.cloudwatch_basic attaches that wildcard policy to the same aws_iam_role.gerrit_instance used by host_logs_ship
advisory.finding: The new host_logs_ship IAM policy is scoped to one log group ARN, but the same instance role already carries the cloudwatch_basic inline policy granting logs:CreateLogGroup/CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents on resources=["*"]; the broad wildcard still applies, so the advertised least-privilege scoping of host_logs_ship has no real effect on the role's effective log permissions.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a _config_problems check (and seeded-defect test) asserting the journald init.scope / {instance_id}/systemd source is shipped.
evidence: host_logs.tf comment: 'The agent ships journald (kernel, docker.service ... nginx, systemd unit-failure lines)'
_config_problems only iterates for unit in ("docker.service", "nginx.service", "rebar-*") — 'init.scope' / the /systemd stream is never asserted
ABSENCE: no test among test_agent_config_* references init.scope or the /systemd stream
advisory.finding: The agent config's journald 'init.scope' (systemd unit start/stop/failure) source is shipped and documented as the /systemd stream, but no test asserts it; _config_problems only checks docker.service, nginx.service, rebar-* and the kernel match, so dropping the init.scope collect_list entry would not fail any test.
scenarios: A refactor or edit removes the init.scope collect_list entry, silently losing systemd unit-failure lines off-box; all tests still pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _config_problems, add 'init.scope' to the required-units loop (or a dedicated check for the {instance_id}/systemd stream), and add a test_seeded_missing_systemd_source_is_rejected companion.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the CloudWatch agent version should be pinned (version parameter on AWS-ConfigureAWSPackage) to make the production host's agent version deterministic and reviewable.
evidence: host_logs.tf:66-69: parameters = { action = "Install", name = "AmazonCloudWatchAgent" } with no version parameter
host_logs.tf:6-10 comment explicitly states 'version unpinned, so AWS keeps it current'
dropped.finding: The CloudWatch agent is installed by AWS-ConfigureAWSPackage with no version pin on a daily schedule against the production Gerrit host, so the agent binary version on the production box can change automatically whenever AWS publishes a new default, with no change recorded in Terraform state (uncontrolled drift / blast radius on a single prod host).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider setting optionalRestart to "no" (or making the configure association change-driven rather than hourly) to avoid recurring restart-induced shipping gaps on the production host.
evidence: host_logs.tf:77-78 comment: 'Re-applying hourly restarts the agent once an hour'
dropped.finding: The configure association restarts the agent every hour (optionalRestart = "yes" on an hourly cron), introducing a recurring short log-shipping interruption on every run while the host_logs_not_arriving alarm treats a 15-minute empty window as breaching.
